# A dimension-independent conditional relative-entropy upper bound for depolarization

24 October 2026. Independently reconstructed from the root's proposed proof. This argument is self-contained in finite-dimensional metric and entropy identities and uses no N675 undecidability or order-equivalence claim. External historical priority is not established.

## Theorem

Let A have dimension d≥2, let 0≤λ≤1, and define depolarization

D_λ(X)=λX+(1−λ)Tr(X)I_A/d.

For every finite reference R and faithful states ρ_AR,σ_AR,

D((D_λ⊗id_R)(ρ)||(D_λ⊗id_R)(σ))−D(ρ_R||σ_R)
≤ c_d(λ)[D(ρ||σ)−D(ρ_R||σ_R)],

where

c_d(λ)=(d²−1)λ²/[1+(d²−2)λ].                         (1)

Consequently the conditional Umegaki contraction coefficient is at most c_d(λ). For d=2 and λ=1/2, the bound is 3/8. For 0<λ<1, c_d(λ)<λ, so it improves the direct mixture/Doeblin bound λ. Equality of the exact coefficient with (1) is not claimed.

The same inequality extends by common faithful regularization to finite-dimensional pairs for which all relative entropies displayed here are finite. Infinite-minus-infinite expressions are not defined by this note.

## Definitions and normalization

For a faithful state a, define Ω_a(X)=(aX+Xa)/2 and

g^S_a(H)=Tr H Ω_a^(−1)(H).

This is the SLD metric, with spectral kernel 2/(a_i+a_j). Define the BKM metric by

g^B_a(H)=Tr H Dlog_a(H),

whose spectral kernel is (log a_i−log a_j)/(a_i−a_j), with diagonal value 1/a_i. For a bipartite baseline σ and Hermitian tangent H, put

Q^S_σ(H)=g^S_σ(H)−g^S_{σ_R}(H_R),
Q^B_σ(H)=g^B_σ(H)−g^B_{σ_R}(H_R).

These are nonnegative by data processing under the partial trace. They are conditional metric deficits, not the unrestricted full-metric ratio, which has a reference-only direction with contraction one.

## Step 1: exact SLD reference gauge

For arbitrary Hermitian H, set

L=Ω_{σ_R}^(−1)(H_R),
V=Ω_σ(I_A⊗L),
H₀=H−V.

Partial trace gives H₀,R=H_R−Ω_{σ_R}(L)=0. The SLD bilinear pairing satisfies

⟨H₀,V⟩_σ=Tr H₀(I_A⊗L)=Tr H₀,R L=0.

Furthermore

g^S_σ(V)=Tr σ(I_A⊗L)²=Tr σ_R L²=g^S_{σ_R}(H_R).

Hence

Q^S_σ(H)=g^S_σ(H₀).                                  (2)

Let Φ act on A only. Because multiplication by a reference observable commutes with Φ⊗id_R,

Φ_R(V)=Ω_{Φ_R(σ)}(I_B⊗L).

The output reference marginal is still σ_R, so the same L is its reference gauge. Thus

Q^S_{Φ_R(σ)}(Φ_R(H))=g^S_{Φ_R(σ)}(Φ_R(H₀)).           (3)

# Independent verification: simplex witnesses attain the complete conditional bound

24 October 2026. This is an analytic check plus a separate dense-matrix audit. Historical priority and external proof review remain open.

## Exact result checked

For N>=2, 0<=λ<=1, and the N-symbol uniform-reset channel K_{λ,N},
ηc_D(K_{λ,N})=ηΔ_D(K_{λ,N})=(N−1)λ²/[1+(N−2)λ].

Here ηc optimizes ordinary relative-entropy contraction over pairs with equal untouched reference marginals; ηΔ optimizes reference-subtracted relative-entropy contraction over arbitrary pairs. The existing conditional upper proof handles arbitrary finite quantum references. The construction below gives the matching LOWER bound using equal-marginal pairs with reference dimensionN.

Consequently exact Weyl/Bell transfer at N=d² gives
ηc_D(D_{λ,d})=ηΔ_D(D_{λ,d})=(d²−1)λ²/[1+(d²−2)λ]
for quantum depolarization of physical dimensiond. A reference of dimensiond³ suffices to approach both suprema. Neither equality for arbitrary channels nor an equality with the unconditioned mutual-information coefficient follows.

## Explicit simplex and positivity

Work in R=C^N. Let u=(1,...,1)/sqrtN and
v_i=(e_i−(1/N)(1,...,1))/sqrt(1−1/N), i=1,...,N.
Then ||v_i||=1, <u,v_i>=0, Σ_i v_i=0, and
(1/N)Σ_i |v_i><v_i|=P_{u⊥}/(N−1).

For 0<ε<1 put σ_i=(1−ε)|v_i><v_i|+(ε/N)I_R and X_i=|v_i><u|+|u><v_i|. Define cq baseline σ=(1/N)⊕_i σ_i and tangent H=(1/N)⊕_i X_i. Every σ_i has trace one, every X_i has trace zero, and Σ_i X_i=0. Thus H_R=0 EXACTLY, not merely asymptotically. The joint baseline is faithful with minimum eigenvalue ε/N².

Write a=1−ε+ε/N and b=ε/N. In span{v_i,u}, σ_i+tX_i has matrix [[a,t],[t,b]], so it is positive definite exactly when |t|<sqrt(ab). Outside this span its eigenvalue is b. Thus every sufficiently small nonzero t gives actual faithful states ρ_t=σ+tH and σ with exactly the same reference marginal.

## Exact BKM ratio

The reference marginal is τ=(1−ε)P_{u⊥}/(N−1)+(ε/N)I. After K, the normalized block is σ_i'=λσ_i+(1−λ)τ and tangent λX_i. On span{v_i,u}, its eigenvalues are
 a'=(1−ε)c+b, b'=b,
where c=λ+(1−λ)/(N−1).

With L(a,b)=(log a−log b)/(a−b), the BKM form of X_i is2L(a,b); all other components vanish. Homogeneity gives g^B_{σ_i/N}(X_i/N)=g^B_{σ_i}(X_i)/N, so averaging N blocks introduces no extra factor. Therefore

g^B_{Kσ}(KH)/g^B_σ(H)
= λ²/c · log[1+N(1−ε)c/ε]/log[1+N(1−ε)/ε].

# Independent reconstruction of simplex sharpness

24 October 2026. This proof independently verifies the root's construction. It uses the established conditional group-twirl upper bound, not N675 or an assumed metric-order equivalence. Historical priority is not asserted.

## 1. Classical uniform-reset channel with a quantum reference

Let N≥2 and 0<λ<1. Consider K_{λ,N}=λI_N+(1−λ)J_N/N. Let the reference be R=C|0>⊕V with dim V=N−1. Choose unit regular-simplex vectors v₁,…,v_N∈V, satisfying

∑_i v_i=0,
(1/N)∑_i |v_i><v_i|=I_V/(N−1).

For example, realize V as the zero-sum subspace of C^N and take v_i=sqrt(N/(N−1))(e_i−(1/N)∑_j e_j), adjoining the orthogonal vacuum |0> as the remaining direction.

For 0<ε<1, define faithful reference states and Hermitian coherence tangents

σ_i=(1−ε)|v_i><v_i|+εI_R/N,
X_i=|v_i><0|+|0><v_i|.

Set the cq baseline and tangent to

Σ=(1/N)⊕_i σ_i,
H=(1/N)⊕_i X_i.

Every block is faithful. The marginal tangent is exactly zero because ∑_iX_i=0. The baseline marginal is

τ_R=(1−ε)I_V/(N−1)+εI_R/N.

Thus (Σ+tH,Σ) has identical reference marginals for every sufficiently small real t, not merely to leading order. Positivity holds whenever t²<ab, where a=1−ε+ε/N and b=ε/N, since each perturbed block has only the 2×2 nontrivial sector spanned by v_i and |0>.

The output block is σ_i′=λσ_i+(1−λ)τ_R and the normalized block tangent is λX_i. Define

c=λ+(1−λ)/(N−1).

On the v_i,|0> sector, the output baseline eigenvalues are

a′=(1−ε)c+ε/N,
b=ε/N.

This is an exact eigenbasis statement: τ_R is scalar on all of V, and the vacuum is orthogonal to V. There is no perturbative approximation or simultaneous-diagonalization assumption across different i.

## 2. Exact BKM quotient

For a diagonal 2×2 baseline diag(a,b) and tangent X with two offdiagonal entries equal to one,

g^B_{diag(a,b)}(X)=2(log a−log b)/(a−b).

The input cq metric equals the average of the normalized block metrics: g_{σ_i/N}(X_i/N)=(1/N)g_{σ_i}(X_i). All normalized blocks have the same metric, so the overall quotient is exactly

q_ε = (λ²/c)
  log[1+N(1−ε)c/ε] / log[1+N(1−ε)/ε].                (1)

Since c>0 is fixed,

lim_{ε→0} q_ε = λ²/c
 = (N−1)λ²/[1+(N−2)λ].                              (2)
